title: Why does the bank pay YOU interest? 🏦
description:
One deposit, one baker, one bigger oven: the simplest way to see where the interest on your savings actually comes from.

Rates in the video are example numbers. Sources: Reserve Bank of Australia, 'What are interest margins?'; Capital One, 'How does savings interest work?'

meta.topic: why banks pay interest on deposits (net interest margin)

humour.trend: 'how X acts 0.1 seconds after...' captions from the Skull Cap trend (rising, late Oct-Nov 2026)

speaker: ved

scenes.say: Why does a bank *pay you*... just for keeping your money there?
Sounds way too generous, right? Here's the trick.
Amina puts *100 coins* in the bank.
The bank keeps a few safe in the vault...
...and *lends* the rest to Ravi, the baker.
Ravi buys a bigger oven... and bakes *twice* the bread.
Business booms! So he pays the bank back... *plus interest*.
Say Ravi pays *8%*. The bank gives Amina *3%*... and keeps the *gap*.

scenes.say: Amina earns. Ravi grows. The bank profits.
So interest isn't a gift. It's *rent*... for borrowing your money.
